doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Road memories, photos, neighborhood and church
title: The Howard Theater in Washington and the numbers hit
summary: Hinton recalls Howard Theater dates, an upstairs club, and winning about $800 on a number from his mother's address.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Do you have any memories of Washington, D.C. in terms of playing there?
Yeah, I played at the Howard Theater there. I always played the Howard. I never played any places but the Howard or a dance, and I…
Where did you play the dances, do you remember? Was it the Colonnade, did you play there or the Masonic…
It sounds like the Masonic place. And there was a place across [unintelligible] where the Howard Theater was.
The Howard Theater was 7th and T.
7th and T. Across the street from the Howard Theater was some kind of little nightclub upstairs.
Right, right. And that was right around the corner of 7th and T.
There was guy named Jerome who sang.

We used to go up there to hear him. And the restaurant around the corner was great. I really enjoyed that [unintelligible]. We stayed… I can‟t remember the lady‟s name where we stayed, because we stayed at somebody‟s house and we stayed there every time we came to Washington, D.C. I was back in those days somewhat of a gambler and I remember coming out of the theater one day… numbers was a big thing down there. And I played… it was Paul Webster, my dear friend Paul [unintelligible]. I played a number… my mother‟s address in Chicago, 403. I played it and Paul… I was going to put a quarter on it, Paul said, “Put a dollar on it, here”. I said, “No, I‟ve got a dollar”, so I put a dollar on it, the number came up and it played something like 800 to 1, $800 bucks. Well $800 bucks was… we had a party in the basement of the Howard Theater. I bought booze, I gave to Hilton Jefferson, my friend, $50, and Kay Johnson $50, and Paul Webster $50. Paul said to me… I‟ve got all this money. I sent my mother some money

and everything… drank as much as we possibly could. Paul said to me, “You know, why don‟t you put a dollar on that number for tomorrow”. I said, “You‟re crazy. We won the money. I ain‟t going to put no dollar”. He said, “You never can tell”. I didn‟t put a dollar. The number came back the next day the same way. I didn‟t have five cents on it [laughter]. I think I‟d better give up numbers.
